questions.q: Which SQL Server feature does this lesson use to pull a table's structural metadata automatically?
options: INFORMATION_SCHEMA views
The Windows Event Viewer
A manually maintained Excel spreadsheet
The sp_helpdb stored procedure exclusively
questions.explain: Querying INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS returns column name, data type, length, nullability, and default value directly from the live schema, with no manual documentation effort.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what can't INFORMATION_SCHEMA tell you about a column like IsActiveFlag?
options: What the column means in business terms — that has to be written by a person
The column's data type
Whether the column allows NULL values
The column's default value
questions.explain: INFORMATION_SCHEMA reports structural facts automatically, but the business meaning of a column — why it exists and how it's used — requires a human to write it, the same way Lesson 2 established for business metadata generally.

questions.q: What does sp_addextendedproperty do, per this lesson?
options: Attaches a human-written description directly to a database object, so it lives with the object itself
Deletes a column from a table permanently
Automatically generates business definitions using AI
Changes a column's data type
questions.explain: Extended properties attach documentation directly to a schema, table, or column, so it shows up in SSMS's Object Explorer and travels with the database instead of living in a separate document.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say attaching a description via an extended property is better than keeping it in a separate spreadsheet?
options: Because the description lives with the object itself, instead of a separate document that can drift out of sync
Because spreadsheets cannot store any text longer than ten characters
Because extended properties are the only way to query a database at all
Because SQL Server deletes spreadsheets automatically
questions.explain: A separate spreadsheet inevitably goes stale as the database changes; an extended property stored directly on the object stays attached to it.

questions.q: In the worked combined entry, which fields come from INFORMATION_SCHEMA versus requiring a human to write them?
options: Column name and data type come from INFORMATION_SCHEMA automatically; the description requires a human to write it
All fields, including the description, are generated automatically with no human involvement
Only the owner field is automatic; everything else requires manual entry
Nothing in a dictionary entry can ever be automated
questions.explain: Structural facts (name, type, nullability, default) come free from the database schema itself; the human-written description and owner assignment still require a person.
